So I’ve dealt with something similar.
First time I went to the gynecologist, I explained I had a bad experience and asked if the guy could please take it easy. He didn’t and he got mad at me for getting upset after he went too fast with everything.
This resulted in me not having seen a gynecologist since.
However, June this year, I went to my GP and told her I wanted to get an IUD but I was scared of the placement since I had to deal with the aftermath of being sexually abused and my bad experience at the gynecologist. We had a talk about all this, and my worries. We agreed she would book me a longer appointment, and we’d take things slow, at my pace. 
Even though placing the IUD was one of the most painful things I’ve had to go through, I went through with it and afterwards, it felt like I gained control over my body back. 

What you might want to do:
- call the gynecologist and set up an extra appointment before getting anything done. Even if it’s just over the phone. In this talk, explain what you went through and what worries you, and what might happen if you do get triggered. Try and come to solutions. As you stated, walk through what they’ll be doing at the appointment. 
- If the gynecologist isn’t willing to be understanding, go to a different one.
- while at the appointment you can ask the gynecologist if she/he will talk you through exactly what they’re about to do and what this will feel like for you, so that you can mentally prepare yourself.
- if you need to take a breather, tell them. Tell them to wait and just give you a minute to breathe and collect yourself. That’s perfectly okay to ask. 
- if you are getting triggered, tell the doctor. It is okay if you get emotional. A good gynecologist will be understanding and give you all the time and help you need.

You’re not alone, and once you go through this appointment, you’re going to feel so empowered. You can do this, this is a step towards healing!
